hints: Focus on what is different between reaction 1 and reaction 2, the concentration of the acid while everything else stays the same.
Reaction 2 uses $0.5 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ acid compared to only $0.1 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ in reaction 1, so think about which one has more $\text{H}^{+}$ particles per $\text{cm}^{3}$ to collide.
Remember that initial rate is directly linked to how many effective collisions happen per second, so both ratios will point the same way when you put reaction 1 on top.
walkthrough:
**Compare the two conditions**

Think like a teacher watching the particles. Both use the same mass of the same $\text{CuCO}_{3}$ powder and acid in excess, so surface area and amount of solid are not the difference.

The only change is: $$\text{Reaction 1: } 0.1 \text{ mol dm}^{-3} \text{ HNO}_{3} \quad \text{vs} \quad \text{Reaction 2: } 0.5 \text{ mol dm}^{-3} \text{ HNO}_{3}$$

**Link concentration to collisions and rate**

Higher acid concentration means more $\text{H}^{+}(\text{aq})$ ions crowded into the same $50 \text{ cm}^{3}$ volume. That gives a higher frequency of collisions with the $\text{CuCO}_{3}$ surface, and so more effective collisions per second.

Collision theory tells us:
$$\text{higher concentration} \rightarrow \text{more effective collisions per second} \rightarrow \text{faster initial rate}$$ 
So reaction 2 is faster than reaction 1.

**Evaluate the two ratios**

Since rate 1 is smaller than rate 2:
$$\frac{\text{rate of reaction 1}}{\text{rate of reaction 2}} < 1$$
And since effective collisions per second follow the rate exactly:
$$\frac{\text{initial effective collisions in 1 per second}}{\text{initial effective collisions in 2 per second}} < 1$$
Both values are less than 1.

options.A: Incorrect. This says both ratios are greater than 1, meaning reaction 1 is faster. That is backwards because the more dilute $0.1 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ acid cannot give a faster rate than the more concentrated $0.5 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ acid.
options.B: Incorrect. This says rate 1 / rate 2 is greater than 1 but collisions ratio is less than 1. That is impossible because rate is proportional to effective collisions per second, so the two ratios must be on the same side of 1. It also wrongly makes the dilute acid faster.
options.C: Incorrect. This correctly says rate 1 / rate 2 is less than 1, but then says the collisions ratio is greater than 1. Students choosing this forget that initial rate and number of effective collisions per second rise and fall together.
options.D: Correct. Reaction 2 has 5 times the $\text{HNO}_{3}$ concentration, so it has more effective collisions per second and a faster initial rate of $\text{CO}_{2}$ production. Therefore both rate 1 / rate 2 and collisions 1 / collisions 2 are less than 1.
